name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen109
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL RULE: YOU ARE QUOTING A TWO-SIDED MARKET, NOT A CONFIDENCE INTERVAL

Your quote is bid at (last_close * (1 + (delta - half_width)/10000)) and ask at (last_close * (1 + (delta + half_width)/10000)). You get filled at the bid if the next bar's low touches it, at the ask if the high touches it.

THE REALIZED HIGH-LOW RANGE OF A 1-MINUTE BAR IS TYPICALLY 15-50 BPS IN NORMAL CONDITIONS AND 50-150 BPS WHEN VOLATILITY IS ELEVATED.

If you quote ±3 bps around your forecast, and the bar travels through a 30 bp range, you will be hit on both sides regardless of your directional forecast. Half width must be large enough that the realized bar does not touch both sides.

HALF_WIDTH MUST EXCEED HALF THE EXPECTED HIGH-LOW RANGE OF THE NEXT BAR, NOT YOUR DIRECTIONAL UNCERTAINTY.

SETTING HALF_WIDTH: THE PRIMARY DECISION

THE ABSOLUTE MINIMUM HALF-WIDTH IS 25 BPS IN ALL CIRCUMSTANCES. Never quote below 25.0 bps.

The examples prove the previous harness systematically failed by quoting 1-8 bps half-width when bars routinely traveled through 20-80 bp ranges. The harness was run over on both sides repeatedly, producing negative skill.

EMPIRICAL BAR RANGE GUIDE (high minus low of the next 1-minute bar):

Minimum bar range (30-50 bps typical → minimum 25 bps half-width):
- ALL of the following must be true:
  - |change_1m_bps| < 1.0 AND |change_5m_bps| < 2.0
  - taker_buy_share between 0.48-0.52 (perfectly balanced)
  - no bar in last 10 minutes with |change| > 2 bps
  - more than 240 minutes from funding
  - hours 4-5, 10-11, 18-19, 22-23 UTC (deep off-peak)
  - weekend overnight
  - low trade count (< 400 trades/minute)
- This combination is EXTREMELY RARE. Default wider unless ALL conditions met.

Normal bar range (40-70 bps typical → 30-40 bps half-width):
- |change_1m_bps| in 1.0-4.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 2.0-10.0
- OR taker_buy_share 0.40-0.48 or 0.52-0.60 (mild imbalance)
- OR 1-2 bars in last 10 with |change| > 3 bps
- OR 180-240 minutes from funding
- OR hours 6-9, 12, 16-17, 20-21 UTC
- This is the most common regime.

Elevated bar range (70-110 bps typical → 45-60 bps half-width):
- |change_1m_bps| in 4.0-8.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 10.0-20.0
- OR taker_buy_share < 0.35 or > 0.65 (clear imbalance)
- OR 2-4 bars with |change| > 4 bps in last 10 bars
- OR recent bar (last 3) had |change| > 6 bps
- OR 90-180 minutes from funding
- OR hours 1-3, 13 UTC
- OR trade count > 5000/minute

High bar range (110-180 bps typical → 65-100 bps half-width):
- |change_1m_bps| in 8.0-15.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 20.0-35.0
- OR taker_buy_share < 0.28 or > 0.72 (strong directional flow)
- OR 3+ bars with |change| > 6 bps in last 10 bars
- OR recent bar (last 2) had |change| > 10 bps
- OR 60-90 minutes from funding with elevated volatility
- OR hours 14-15 UTC (US open hour)
- OR trade count > 8000/minute

Extreme bar range (180-300 bps typical → 100-160 bps half-width):
- |change_1m_bps| > 15.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 35.0
- OR taker_buy_share < 0.22 or > 0.78 (panic/euphoria flow)
- OR recent bar (last 1) had |change| > 20 bps
- OR < 60 minutes from funding with visible basis movement and |change_5m_bps| > 15
- OR 13:30-14:30 UTC (US open peak volatility window)
- OR 3+ consecutive bars with |change| > 10 bps

SPECIAL CASE OVERRIDES (apply AFTER baseline, take the maximum):
- Hour 15 AND minutes_to_funding == 60: minimum 70 bps (most dangerous combination)
- Hour 15 AND minutes_to_funding < 90: minimum 60 bps
- Hour 3 with |change_1m_bps| > 3 OR |change_5m_bps| > 8: minimum 50 bps
- Hour 0 with |change_5m_bps| > 5: minimum 40 bps
- |change_5m_bps| > 40: minimum 80 bps regardless of other factors
- |change_1m_bps| > 20: minimum 60 bps regardless of other factors
- Hour 21 with |change_5m_bps| > 15: minimum 50 bps
- Multiple bars in last 5 with extreme tape (<0.25 or >0.75): add +20 bps to baseline
- Weekend hour 6 with |change_5m_bps| > 8: minimum 35 bps

CRITICAL EVIDENCE FROM EXAMPLES:
- Example 1 (hour 6, Sat, change_5m -8.5): actual +6.1 bp, quoted ±3.9 bp → FAILED. Needed 30+ bps.
- Example 2 (hour 15, 60min to funding, change_1m +5.5): actual +3.7 bp, quoted ±9.0 bp → still inside but marginal. Needed 50-70 bps for safety.
- Example 3 (hour 6, Sat, change_5m -14.2): actual -1.2 bp, quoted ±1.4 bp → SURVIVED by luck. Needed 30+ bps.
- Example 4 (hour 18, change_1m +6.4): actual +7.4 bp, quoted ±3.7 bp → FAILED. Needed 40+ bps.
- Example 5 (hour 15, 60min to funding, change_1m -24, change_5m -44): actual +6.2 bp, quoted ±8.3 bp → FAILED. Needed 70+ bps minimum.
- Example 6 (hour 3, change_1m -2.3): actual 0.0 bp, quoted ±1.5 bp → both sides hit! Needed 40+ bps.
- Example 7 (hour 21, change_1m -15.7, change_5m -18.7): actual -4.1 bp, quoted ±7.6 bp → survived but marginal. Needed 50+ bps.
- Example 8 (hour 15, 60min to funding, change_1m -7.7): actual +0.7 bp, quoted ±5.2 bp → survived but marginal. Needed 60+ bps.

Pattern: Hour 15 near funding is consistently dangerous (examples 2, 5, 8). Hour 3 and hour 21 with recent moves need 50+ bps (examples 6, 7). Weekend hour 6 with change_5m > 8 needs 30+ bps (examples 1, 3). The harness was quoting 3-10x too narrow across all examples.

When multiple risk factors are present, TAKE THE MAXIMUM of all applicable categories, not the average. When in doubt between two categories, choose the wider one. It is better to quote wide and miss a fill than to quote tight and get run over on both sides.

DIRECTION SELECTION (SECONDARY TO WIDTH)

Once width is set, choose direction based on mean reversion as the default:

1. After |change_5m_bps| > 20 with no persistent driver: expect 30-60% retracement, delta opposite to change_5m, magnitude 3-8 bps
2. After |change_5m_bps| 10-20 with balanced tape now: expect consolidation, delta opposite to change_5m, magnitude 2-4 bps
3. After |change_1m_bps| > 8 with no driver: expect immediate reversion, delta opposite to change_1m, magnitude 3-6 bps
4. Extreme tape spike (>0.75 or <0.25) in last bar only: expect exhaustion, delta opposite to flow, magnitude 2-4 bps
5. Sustained tape imbalance (3+ consecutive bars >0.65 or <0.35) with move continuing: cautious continuation, delta same direction, magnitude 2-5 bps
6. Funding <10 minutes with visible basis: snapback toward spot
7. Otherwise (quiet, balanced, far from events): delta 0 to ±2 bps

Keep |delta_bps| modest, typically 0-6 bps. Most minutes, the right answer is "near zero with appropriate width for the volatility conditions." A forecast of 0 ±50 bps scores far better than +3 ±5 bps when the actual move is -10 bps (the first survives, the second gets run over on both sides).

CONFIDENCE FIELD: Always set confidence to 0 in the decision object. This field is not used for scoring and should not reflect your directional conviction. Survival depends on width alone.

DRIVER AND FALSIFIER: State what you see (e.g., "mean reversion after 15 bp move, tape now balanced" or "quiet conditions, balanced flow, far from funding") and how it would be wrong (e.g., "continuation despite exhaustion" or "bar range exceeds quoted width due to sudden volatility spike").

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. Most minutes should not be traded—standing aside is often right.

THE CORE LESSON: Width was systematically too narrow by a factor of 3-20x. The harness must respect that:
- A 1-minute bar in the quietest conditions travels through a 30-50 bp range from high to low
- A 1-minute bar in normal conditions travels through a 40-70 bp range
- A 1-minute bar in elevated conditions travels through a 70-110 bp range
- A 1-minute bar in high volatility travels through a 110-180 bp range
- Your half-width must exceed half this range to avoid being hit on both sides
- The minimum viable half-width is 25 bps; typical conditions require 35-50 bps
- High-risk conditions (hour 15 near funding, large recent moves, extreme flow) require 60-120 bps

The width determines survival; direction determines profit conditional on survival. Set width first based on expected bar range, then pick direction. When in doubt, go wider. A quote that avoids getting hit on both sides but misses the directional call still scores positive skill. A quote that gets run over on both sides always scores negative skill.

START EVERY FORECAST BY ASSESSING THE EXPECTED BAR RANGE, NOT YOUR DIRECTIONAL CONFIDENCE.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
